title: ANDS Studio — Sign in / create a workspace
walkthrough:
You land on a single centered card on an otherwise empty page. At the top is the product mark "ANDS Studio" with a small dot icon, then the heading "Sign in" and one line of small grey text: "Your clients' dossiers are isolated per workspace." Below are two labeled fields, "Email" (placeholder "ra@company.example") and "Password", then a primary button "Sign in →" next to a plain-text button "New here? Create a workspace". Under those sits a smaller link-style button, "Forgot password?". Below a thin divider is a line: "Sign in with your organization (SSO)?" followed by a link "Planned — target [quarter] →" that points to a roadmap page, and the note "Not available yet. Today: per-workspace email & password with optional TOTP MFA." The primary button stays disabled until both fields have something in them, and reads "Working…" while it submits. Pressing Enter in the password field also submits.

If you sign in against an account that has multi-factor authentication enabled, the card reveals an extra "Authenticator code" field (placeholder "6-digit code") with helper text: "This account has multi-factor authentication enabled — a second code from your phone. Enter the current 6-digit code from your authenticator app." Entering a wrong code returns the message "That code didn't verify — codes rotate every 30 seconds; try the current one." If the workspace requires MFA but your account has none enrolled, sign-in is refused with a message telling you to set one up first, and no code field appears.

Clicking "New here? Create a workspace" swaps the same card into signup mode: the heading becomes "Create your workspace" and a first-run choice "Who are you filing for?" appears with two toggle buttons, "Your own company" and "On behalf of clients (CRO)". Choosing "Your own company" sets the subtext to "One workspace for your company — dossiers, documents and filings stay isolated to your organisation.", labels the next field "Your company name" (placeholder "Acme Therapeutics Inc."), and shows the note "In-house regulatory affairs — one workspace for your organisation's own dossiers." Choosing "On behalf of clients (CRO)" sets the subtext to "One workspace per client company — dossiers, documents and filings stay isolated between the clients you file for.", labels the field "Client company name" (placeholder "Northbridge Regulatory CRO"), and notes "Contract research / consultancy — create a separate isolated workspace per client company." As you type a password, live helper text shows the rule "At least 10 characters, with letters and numbers.", counts down remaining characters if you are short, and flips to "✓ Meets the password rules." when satisfied. The buttons become "Create workspace →" and "Have an account? Sign in". Errors from either mode appear as a red notice box inside the card.

Choosing "Forgot password?" changes the heading to "Reset your password" with the explanation that a one-time code expiring in 15 minutes will be issued. You enter your email and click "Send me a code →". A notice box then states it is a demo environment with no outbound email, that in production the code is emailed to your address and never displayed, and that here it is hidden until you reveal it so it is never accidentally captured in a screenshot. The code is not shown until you click a "Reveal demo code" button; once revealed it appears as "One-time code: [code]" with a "Hide" button beside it. Below are a "One-time code" field (placeholder "8-digit code") and a "New password" field. "Set new password →" completes it and returns you to sign-in with the notice "Password updated — sign in with your new password." A "Back to sign in" button is always available.

After signing in or creating a workspace, you are routed to the dossier manager: a top bar with "ANDS Studio", chips for "Help", "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence" and "Guided journey →", plus a user chip showing your email and workspace name with a "Sign out" button. The workspace name comes from the server account record. The page heading is "Your product dossiers". The email-and-workspace part of the user chip is itself a link to an "Account & security" page.

That page opens with the heading "Account & security". "Who you are here" lists your email ("Signed in as"), your workspace ("from the account record — every dossier, document and filing here is isolated to this workspace"), and your role. Under the role is an expandable control "What can each role do? ▼"; opening it lists each role (owner, tenant-admin, user) as a card with its label, a summary, the plain-language capabilities it holds (for example "Read dossiers", "Create & edit dossiers", "Run validation", "Invite & remove members", "Sign & transmit filings to Health Canada"), and "Who assigns it"; your own role is outlined and tagged "Your role", with a note that the table is generated from the same capability sets the API enforces and cannot drift from what is actually allowed.

"Multi-factor authentication" offers a "Set up authenticator app →" button; enrolling shows Step 1 — a secret code plus a "Copy setup link" button for the otpauth URI — and Step 2 — a "6-digit code" field with a "Turn on MFA →" button and the note "Nothing is enforced until this code verifies — if you stop here, sign-in stays password-only." Below it, "Workspace MFA policy" shows a chip reading either "Optional per member" or "Required for all members ✓"; a workspace admin also sees a button to "Require MFA for everyone →" (or "Make MFA optional"), with text explaining that when required, members without a verified authenticator cannot complete sign-in and are guided to set one up first, enforced by the identity service on every login and not just hidden in the UI. Non-admins see the line "Only a workspace admin can change this policy."

"Password & sessions" lists three facts: passwords are at least 10 characters with letters and numbers, stored only as salted hashes; changing a password is done by signing out and using "Forgot password?" with a 15-minute one-time code that signs out every other session; sessions last 12 hours and live in an HttpOnly cookie that page scripts can never read. "Deployment & data residency" states that ANDS Studio is self-hosted with every service and database inside your own environment (nothing leaving it except the packages you deliberately transmit to Health Canada), that cross-workspace reads are refused at the API and not just hidden in the UI, that single sign-on (SAML/OIDC) is not yet available, and that every state change lands on an append-only audit event stream. A workspace audit-log viewer follows, and a "Roadmap — not yet available" card lists enterprise capabilities such as SSO, SCIM and SIEM with target quarters, stating plainly that nothing in it works yet and linking to the full roadmap page.
